target.title: fix(qqbot): add 30s request timeout to token endpoint fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`TokenManager.doFetchToken()` calls `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without a `timeoutMs` deadline. The QQBot token endpoint (`bots.qq.com/app/getAppAccessToken`) could accept the TCP connection but never return response headers, causing the token fetch to hang indefinitely and block all QQBot API communication.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `QQBOT_TOKEN_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` applied to the `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call inside `doFetchToken()`.

30s matches the established REST API timeout convention across the codebase (mattermost, msteams, googlechat request timeouts, and other extensions).

**Scope — only the token endpoint:**

| Path | Status |
|------|--------|
| `TokenManager.doFetchToken()` -> `fetchWithSsrFGuard` | Fixed |
| qqbot/api-client.ts | Already protected (AbortController) |
| qqbot/media.ts | Already protected (media download timeout) |
| qqbot/stt.ts | Already protected |
| All other qqbot calls | Already protected |

## User Impact

A stalled QQBot token endpoint no longer blocks the plugin indefinitely. Token fetch fails with a timeout-class error after 30s instead of waiting forever. The `TokenManager` retry logic picks up the failure normally and refreshes on the next attempt.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed:** `doFetchToken()` forwarded no deadline to the SSRF-guarded fetch, so a token endpoint that accepts the connection but never responds hangs all QQBot API operations.

**Real behavior proof (hanging loopback server):** `token.loopback.test.ts` starts a real `node:http` server that accepts the connection and never sends response headers, then drives the production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with the forwarded deadline. The request rejects near the deadline instead of remaining pending:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/api/token.loopback.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)

# Standalone measurement of the same guarded-fetch path (timeoutMs = 500):
{"rejectedAfterMs":575,"errorName":"Error","message":"request timed out"}
```

With no deadline the same request stays pending indefinitely; with the forwarded `timeoutMs` it is cut off ~500ms in.

**Wiring proof:** the unit suite asserts `doFetchToken` forwards `timeoutMs: 30_000` to `fetchWithSsrFGuard`:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/api/token.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

**Static checks:** `oxlint` — exit 0; `oxfmt --check` — clean.

**What was not tested:** live QQ platform traffic and a real `bots.qq.com` account were not used. `TOKEN_URL` is fixed and host-scoped, so the hang class is reproduced against a no-response loopback server exercising the same guarded-fetch deadline the production path relies on.

## Root Cause

`TokenManager.doFetchToken()` called `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without a `timeoutMs` — the only remaining qqbot fetch path without deadline protection after `api-client.ts` (AbortController), `media.ts` (media download timeout), and `stt.ts` were already fixed. Fix: add `QQBOT_TOKEN_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` at the call site.

AI-assisted.
